He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton Flyers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Crutcher is the son of Greg and Sheila Crutcher and grew up in [[Memphis, Tennessee]]. He attended [[Ridgeway High School (Memphis, Tennessee)|Ridgeway High School]]. Crutcher averaged 18 points, four assists, and two steals per game as a senior. He was a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] ranked the 65th best point guard in his class.{{cite news|first=Marcus|last=Hartman|title=Meet the Dayton Flyers freshmen: Jalen Crutcher|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/meet-the-dayton-flyers-freshmen-jalen-crutcher/EPGbhVSWa9JFtajtUmUJmM/|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=October 25, 2017|access-date=February 2, 2020}} Crutcher initially committed to [[Chattanooga Mocs men's basketball|Chattanooga]] but decommitted after coach [[Matt McCall (basketball)|Matt McCall]] left to coach [[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass]]. Crutcher signed with [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] after coach [[Anthony Grant (basketball)|Anthony Grant]] needed a point guard at the last minute.{{cite news|first=Tom|last=Archdeacon|title=Archdeacon: 'No moment is too big' for Flyers' Crutcher|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/archdeacon-moment-too-big-for-flyers-crutcher/nWa5n0EQfjZv2vBBbE3PNJ/|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=January 22, 2020|access-date=February 2, 2020}} Crutcher was also recruited by [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State]].{{cite news|first=Tom|last=Archdeacon|title=Archdeacon: A heartfelt hug, no handshake, for Dayton's Grant, Crutcher|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/archdeacon-heartfelt-hug-handshake-for-dayton-grant-crutcher/EKdFJJC6agC87bmodKabVJ/|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=January 14, 2019|access-date=February 2, 2020}} ==College career== As a freshman, Crutcher started 22 games and averaged 9.2 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 4.4 assists per game on a team that finished 14–17.{{cite web|title=MBB Preview: Flyers Coming Together, Rhody Strives for Continuity|url=https://atlantic10.com/news/2018/11/3/211778871.aspx|work=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]]|date=November 3, 2018|access-date=February 2, 2020}} Crutcher was named to the [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] All-[[Rookie]] Team.{{cite press release|title=Aldridge, Adams Named Atlantic 10 Co-Players of Year, Rhode Island's Hurley Voted as Coach of the Year|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=31600&ATCLID=211704410&_ga=2.229189468.1745063048.1520363371-145939181.1520363370|website=Atlantic10.com|publisher=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]]|date=March 6, 2018|access-date=March 6, 2018}} As a sophomore, Crutcher was third on the team in scoring with 13.2 points per game and second in the Atlantic 10 in assists with 5.7 per game, in addition to his four rebounds per game. Crutcher helped the team finish with a 21–12 record and reach the NIT semifinals and he was named team MVP.{{cite news|first=David|last=Jablonski|title=Crutcher named team MVP at Dayton awards banquet|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/crutcher-named-team-mvp-dayton-awards-banquet/gcIuWmdKjlSE9WVyaPam1M/|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=April 11, 2019|access-date=February 2, 2020}}{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Hall|title=Obi Toppin and Jalen Crutcher Are Ready to Lead the Dayton Flyers Back to the NCAA Tournament|url=https://www.bhjournalist.com/post/obi-toppin-and-jalen-crutcher-are-ready-to-lead-the-dayton-flyers-back-to-the-ncaa-tournament|work=BH Journalist|date=September 11, 2019|access-date=February 2, 2020|archive-date=February 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200203034315/https://www.bhjournalist.com/post/obi-toppin-and-jalen-crutcher-are-ready-to-lead-the-dayton-flyers-back-to-the-ncaa-tournament|url-status=dead}} He was also named to the Third Team All-Atlantic 10.{{cite news|title=Gudmondsson named Atlantic 10 Player of the Year, Rhoades voted Coach of the Year|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=31600&ATCLID=211795159|work=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]]|date=March 12, 2019|access-date=March 12, 2019}} Crutcher hit a three-pointer with seconds left against [[2019–20 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] in the final of the [[2019 Maui Invitational Tournament]] to force overtime.{{cite web|first=David|last=Jablonski|title=Dayton guard Jalen Crutcher on game-winning shot: 'Get the ball,' and 'Make a play'|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/jalen-crutcher-final-shot-get-the-ball-and-make-play/XoAzKVKZtTrVJqsma3ZMBN/|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=January 18, 2020|access-date=February 2, 2020}} He scored 12 points total in the 90–84 overtime loss.{{cite web|title=Dayton almost does the thing against No. 4 Kansas, still has statement trip to Maui|url=https://www.midmajormadness.com/2019/11/27/20986404/dayton-kansas-basketball-flyers-maui-jayhawks-upset-obi-toppin-anthony-grant-ranking|website=MidMajorMadness.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=November 27, 2019|access-date=February 2, 2020}} Crutcher missed a game against [[Grambling State Tigers men's basketball|Grambling State]] on December 23 with a concussion.{{cite news|title=Ibi Watson leads No. 18 Dayton over Grambling State 81-53|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2019/12/23/ibi-watson-leads-no-18-dayton-over-grambling-state-81-53/40881095/|work=[[USA Today]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 23, 2019|access-date=February 2, 2020}} On January 17, 2020, Crutcher scored 21 points and hit the game-winning three-pointer at the buzzer to defeat [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis]] 78–76 in overtime.{{cite news|title=Crutcher's 3 in OT lifts No. 13 Dayton over Saint Louis|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401170242|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 17, 2020|access-date=February 2, 2020}}{{cite news|first=Matt|last=Norlander|title=The Court Report: Overlooked national title contender Dayton has surprisingly built an all-time elite offense|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/the-court-report-overlooked-national-title-contender-dayton-has-surprisingly-built-an-all-time-elite-offense/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=January 29, 2020|access-date=February 2, 2020}} Crutcher scored a career-high 24 points and also had eight rebounds and seven assists on January 25, in a 87–79 win over [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball|Richmond]].{{cite news|title=Toppin, Crutcher lead No. 7 Flyers past Richmond, 87-79|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401170257|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 25, 2020|access-date=February 2, 2020}} He became the first Dayton player to be named Atlantic 10 player of the week on back-to-back weeks on January 27.{{cite news|first=David|last=Jablonski|title=Dayton Flyers guard Jalen Crutcher honored by Atlantic 10 for second straight week|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/dayton-flyers-guard-jalen-crutcher-honored-atlantic-for-second-straight-week/oPSRc94fTBlvXOrP5tFD3M/|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=January 27, 2020|access-date=February 2, 2020}} On January 30, he had 18 points in a 73–69 win against [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]] and surpassed the 1,000 point threshold.{{cite news|first=David|last=Jablonski|title=Junior guard scores 18 points points against Duquesne|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/dayton-crutcher-hits-career-milestone-first-half-against-duquesne/yEwIIwuj4867zz0BLPgOLK/|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=January 30, 2020|access-date=February 2, 2020}} At the end of the regular season Crutcher was named to the First Team All-Atlantic 10.{{cite web|first=David|last=Jablonski|title=Obi Toppin makes more Dayton Flyers history in Atlantic 10 awards|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/obi-toppin-makes-more-dayton-flyers-history-atlantic-awards/eOcITCJfq5dixdLyb3NpcP/|work=Dayton Daily News|date=March 10, 2020|access-date=March 10, 2020}} Crutcher led Dayton in minutes per game (33.6), assists per game (4.9) three-pointers (21.4 per game), three-point percentage (.468, 147–314) and free throw percentage (.869, 86–99), and was second to roommate [[Obi Toppin]] in scoring (15.1 points per game).{{cite web|title=Obi Toppin, Jalen Crutcher Named White Allen Co-Most Valuable Players|url=https://daytonflyers.com/news/2020/3/8/mens-basketball-obi-toppin-jalen-crutcher-named-white-allen-co-most-valuable-players.aspx|website=DaytonFlyers.com|date=March 8, 2020 |access-date=March 24, 2020}} After the season, Crutcher declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite news|first=David|last=Jablonski|title=Dayton Flyers guard Jalen Crutcher declares for NBA Draft|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/dayton-flyers-guard-jalen-crutcher-declares-for-nba-draft/DVZ7LUBD55zInuici4EIFK/|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=March 26, 2020|access-date=March 27, 2020}} On August 2, he announced he was withdrawing from the draft and returning to Dayton for his senior season.{{cite news|first=David|last=Jablonski|title=Dayton Flyers: Jalen Crutcher announces his NBA decision|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/dayton-flyers-jalen-crutcher-announces-his-nba-decision/FJM3XPAY4VFZTETFCM7MZ7DULE/|work=[[Dayton Daily News]]|date=August 2, 2020|access-date=August 4, 2020}} At the end of the regular season, Crutcher repeated on the First Team All-Atlantic 10.{{cite news|first=Michael|last=Purves|title=4 Dayton Flyers honored with postseason A-10 Conference awards|url=https://www.whio.com/sports/university-of-dayton-flyers/4-dayton-flyers-honored-with-postseason-a-10-conference-awards/DFULEDDX4ZA5FPR25FLZBLVUUY/|website=WHIO.com|date=March 10, 2021|access-date=June 18, 2021}} As a senior, Crutcher averaged 17.6 points and 4.8 assists per game. He announced that he was declaring for the [[2021 NBA draft]] and hired an agent, forgoing the extra season of eligibility the NCAA granted basketball players. Crutcher finishing 16th in career scoring with 1,593 points, fourth in made three-pointers with 242, and second in assists with 584.{{cite news|title=Dayton star PG Jalen Crutcher to enter NBA Draft|url=https://www.whio.com/sports/jalen-crutcher-will-leave-dayton-enter-nba-draft/OH4CVAHLQZDRJDLZUNXNJL37QQ/|website=WHIO.com|date=May 4, 2021|access-date=June 18, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Greensboro Swarm (2021–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Crutcher joined the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=2021 Bucks Summer League Central|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/summerleague/2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On October 8, 2021, he signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets]],{{cite web|first=Quinton|last=Wash|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Jalen Crutcher and Cameron McGriff|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-sign-jalen-crutcher-and-cameron-mcgriff|website=NBA.com|date=October 8, 2021|access-date=October 8, 2021}} but was waived six days later.{{cite web|title=Hornets Waive Crutcher and McGriff|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-waive-crutcher-and-mcgriff|website=NBA.com|date=October 14, 2021|access-date=October 15, 2021}} On October 24, he signed with the [[Greensboro Swarm]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web|first=Justin|last=Trujillo|title=Swarm Announce Training Camp Roster And Coaching Staff For 2021-22|url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/swarmannouncetrainingcamproster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2021|access-date=October 24, 2021}} ===New Orleans Pelicans / Birmingham Squadron (2023–2024)=== On September 8, 2023, Crutcher's rights were traded to the [[Birmingham Squadron]]{{cite web|title=Birmingham Squadron Acquire Returning Player Rights for Jalen Crutcher from Greensboro|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/birmingham-squadron-acquire-returning-player-rights-for-jalen-crutcher-from-greensboro/n-6011827|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=September 8, 2023|access-date=September 8, 2023}} and on October 12, he signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Jalen Crutcher|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/jalen-crutcher-signed-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-training-camp-2023|website=NBA.com|date=October 12, 2023|access-date=October 12, 2023}} However, he was waived on October 22{{cite web|title=Pelicans Add Matt Ryan On Two-Way Contract|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/pelicans-add-matt-ryan-on-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2023|access-date=November 3, 2023}} and, seven days later, he signed with Birmingham.{{cite web|title=Birmingham Squadron Finalize Training Camp Roster|url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/birmingham-squadron-finalize-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=November 3, 2023}} On February 22, 2024, Crutcher signed a 10-day contract with the Pelicans,{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans announce roster moves|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/malcolm-hill-jalen-crutcher-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-moves-2-22-24|website=NBA.com|date=February 22, 2024|access-date=February 22, 2024}} making his NBA debut on February 27 before returning to Birmingham on March 3.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Birmingham Squadron Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Birmingham-Squadron/59/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 4, 2024}} On September 25, 2024, Crutcher re-signed with the Pelicans,{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Jalen Crutcher|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/jalen-crutcher-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-signing-september-25-2024|website=NBA.com|date=September 25, 2024|access-date=September 26, 2024}} but was waived on October 14.{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Trhae Mitchell|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/trhae-mitchell-guard-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-moves-2024-training-camp-preseason-10-14-24|website=NBA.com|date=October 14, 2024|access-date=October 14, 2024}} On October 28, he rejoined the Squadron.{{cite web|title=Birmingham Squadron Announce 2024-25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/birmingham-squadron-announce-2024-25-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}} On February 26, 2025, the Pelicans signed Crutcher to a two-way contract.{{Cite web|title=Report: Former Dayton guard earns second promotion to NBA|url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/report-former-dayton-guard-earns-second-promotion-to-nba/6KSPJY7TLZCXVM55BGLASCD5OA/|access-date=February 28, 2025|website=daytondailynews.com|language=en}} However, he didn’t appear for the team prior to being waived on March 1.{{Cite web|title=Pelicans Waive Jalen Crutcher|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/03/pelicans-waiving-jalen-crutcher.html|access-date=March 4, 2025|website=hoopsrumors.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics
